Pete Wild has important message to fed-up Hartlepool United fanbase - and explains pre-match move

By Mark Carruthers

Football writer

Published 7th Oct 2026, 06:00 BST

Hartlepool United suffered a 1-0 defeat against National League rivals Tamworth in the first game of Pete Wild’s managerial reign.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:34
Instaread

New Hartlepool United head coach Pete Wild got his first taste of life at Victoria Park in Saturday’s defeat against Tamworth - and immediately set his sights on repairing the disconnect between the club and their fanbase.

The former FC Halifax Town and Barrow boss was officially confirmed as permanent successor to Lee Clark last Thursday and wasted little time in getting to grips with his new squad as he oversaw training on Friday morning before stepping into the dugout at The Vic for a crucial clash with fellow National League strugglers Tamworth just over 24 hours later.

Over 4,000 Poolies were on hand to witness a new era get underway in underwhelming fashion as a goal from visitors striker Kieran Donnelly gave his side all three points and left Pools sitting third from bottom in the table on the back of a run of nine defeats in their last ten games. Wild called on his side to take part in a pre-match huddle in front of supporters ahead of the game as he passed on his final instructions - and he revealed he is determined to ‘repair the disconnect’ between the club and their fans as he looks to guide his side out of the relegation zone during the early weeks of his reign.

Speaking to The Mail after Saturday’s defeat, the new Pools boss said: “I'm a fan, first and foremost, so I know how fans think, and I’ve spent four months watching my club every weekend as a fan. I know how much the fans are important to us, and I know how much the fans care. But it's little things like that [the pre-match huddle in front of supporters] where you're trying, and when I talk about the disconnect between the fans and players, we have to repair that. That's one of many things that I need to do, to try to repair the disconnect. But again, the clubs I've been at, when we've finished our job there, the fans have loved us, and I don't see any difference here.” A visit to Forest Green Rovers on Saturday evening is next on the agenda for Wild and his Pools squad.
